title: Transactions, isolation, concurrency, soft delete
exp: Isolation levels and optimistic concurrency are favorite 4 YOE topics — especially RCSI vs locking.
pts: Read Committed default; Snapshot/RCSI lets readers avoid blocking writers (version store).
Serializable prevents phantoms but costs blocking — use sparingly.
EF: `BeginTransactionAsync` + execution strategy for transient retries.
Soft delete via global filters; watch unique indexes on 'deleted' rows.
pr: Map isolation levels to anomalies they prevent
Add a RowVersion to an Order entity

qa.q: What does READ COMMITTED SNAPSHOT buy you?
qa.a: Row versioning so readers don't take shared locks that block writers (and vice versa) for typical read committed scenarios. Trade-off: tempdb version store cost and different anomaly profile — know it isn't full serializability.

qa.q: How do you handle optimistic concurrency in EF Core?
qa.a: Add a RowVersion/timestamp (or token) configured as concurrency token. On SaveChanges conflict, catch DbUpdateConcurrencyException, reload database values, merge or ask the user, retry.
